title: Otis and the Lost Lullaby Bell
markdown:
The Moonfold Mountains lay like sleeping giants under a deep dark sky, powdered with tiny twinkling stars. From a little round home, snug as a bird’s nest in the soft folds of the hills, a young wizard named Otis looked out. Eyes wide and wondering like a little owl’s, watching the moon’s soft light spill over the sleepy world. Beside him, on the wide windowsill where moonbeams pooled like milk, sat Flicker, a little mouse the warm colour of toasted honey. A happy peep. Whiskers wiggling like tiny feelers at the quiet dance of moonbeams on the floor.

“It’s such a peaceful night, isn’t it, Flicker? But listen. My Lullaby Bell is singing its gentle tune. It always sings when it decides to wander off, and it’s singing much too early for real sleep time.” The Lullaby Bell was Otis’s most special treasure. It was meant to chime only when everyone was deeply, truly sleepy, a soft musical whisper toward dreamland. Sometimes, when Otis was busy with a spell that didn’t quite settle, or watching a funny cloud, the bell would quietly slip from his robe’s little pouch and go on its own journeys.

He smoothed his deep blue robe, a little too big for his small shoulders. He was learning magic, but his spells sometimes had a mind of their own, wiggly, landing with a soft poof instead of a graceful shimmer. Flicker hopped onto his shoulder, warm against his cheek, encouraging peeps, little nose at his ear. “You think we should go and look for it?” A thoughtful line on his brow. Flicker nodded, so full of quiet confidence that Otis felt a little braver. A small hopeful smile, like a moonflower opening. “Alright then. A little exploration it is.”

Flicker tucked in the deep pouch, a warm cozy secret. Otis opened the cottage door. Night air cool and sweet: pine, damp awakened earth. Delicate ferns unfurling like sleepy hands, moonlight making the floor a carpet of green woven with silver. The bell’s chiming faint, a whispered melody on the breeze, from deeper in the whispering trees.

He walked slowly, worn boots hardly a sound on moss that remembered other wanderers and did not tell. He listened with all his might, head tipped like Flicker’s. Sometimes the chime closer, a sweet promise between two pines, then faded, a hiding game among old trees that had practised hiding for years. A moth asked to be the bell and was not. Flicker’s steady peeps from the pouch: not walking alone. A team. Once Otis nearly followed an owl’s question instead of a chime, and Flicker peeped a correction, which is a kind of spell.

Deeper, moonlight in dappled dancing patterns, a soft warm glow ahead. A small clearing. A friendly witch humming a gentle musical tune. Willowisp, kind smile as warm as the lantern on a nearby branch, basket overflowing with herbs that smelled of sunshine and gentle rain. “Hello there, young wizard. Lost something, have we? I hear a faint wandering tune.”

Otis told her about the pouch, and the wiggly spells, and the bell that left when it felt like singing. She listened with a knowing glint. “Ah, the Lullaby Bell. A lively spirit. It likes to sing when it feels a little lonely, or when it finds a particularly interesting mushroom. I have met that sort of mushroom. I can help your looking, just a little.” A sprig of shimmering moonpetal, leaves catching moonlight like tiny stars, cool in his palm. “This will leave a faint sweet scent on the air. A little trail, should the song grow too faint for small wizard ears. Magic often leaves its own delightful clues, if you remember to sniff as well as listen.” Otis thanked her twice, because once felt too thin. Heart lighter. A little wave, graceful, and she returned to her herbs, humming fading like a path you can still taste.

He followed the chiming. The woods grew quieter. The melody danced further away. Moss-glow softened. Tall trees, friendly guardians a moment ago, now whispered secrets he couldn’t quite understand, shadows longer. He strained. The chiming gone, swallowed by deep quiet. A sigh, light as a fallen leaf.

He stopped by a large mossy log, green and grey velvet. No bell at all, as if the night had soaked the melody up. A small worry, no bigger than a butterfly’s flutter, in his tummy. Lost forever this time? The woods a little too vast, a little too deep. A fleeting grey cloud over the moon.

He sat. The log was kinder than it looked. Flicker peeked out, bright beady eyes, concern and affection, one paw on the robe’s rim as if keeping Otis from floating off. Otis stroked the incredibly soft fur, finding comfort in its warmth. “Oh, Flicker. I don’t think we can find it. It’s gone too far.” A comforting peep that always seemed to say we’ll figure it out, even when the woods had eaten the tune. Then a nose-nudge toward a faint sweet aroma drifting on the air, past the grey-cloud feeling, stubborn as a good idea. Moonpetal, just as Willowisp had described. Otis’s eyes widened. Not only a clue. A path. The butterfly-worry folded its wings.

He stood, a tiny spark of hope. Followed the scent, Flicker’s nudges and peeps from the pouch. Past flowers beginning to nod off, under archways of weeping willow, to a patch of shimmering silverleaf, leaves like tiny mirrors. There, nestled among moon-kissed leaves, the Lullaby Bell, golden striker still and quiet. Otis untangled it. As he held it, it chimed a soft sweet perfect lullaby, a happy song of being found. Warmth like sunshine after rain. He thought he heard Willowisp’s humming on the breeze, and whispered thank you in her direction.

Home with the bell now silent and content, Flicker snuggled in the pouch, one whisker still dusted with silverleaf. The moon a big comforting eye. The path familiar and safe, as if the forest had decided the hiding game was over. Ferns tucked their sleepy hands in. The bell was ready for its real job: peaceful dreams, not wander-songs. On a velvety cushion by the fireplace it rested, striker still. Otis hung the moonpetal sprig by the window, in case of future fades. He yawned a big deep sleepy yawn that stretched his little mouth wide. Flicker nested in the robe. Moonlight through the window. Gentle breathing. They drifted off, the bell quiet at last, which is how you know a wander is done.
